Name: The Last Lodge
Supported languages: About The Last Lodge The Last Lodge is a medieval choice-based psychological horror game where you take on the role of an innkeeper—a respected pillar of the community, serving travellers and locals alike. Your duties are clear: tend to your guests, flawlessly prepare their orders, and make your fateful choice when the time comes. However, be exceptionally wary of who comes through your door; your guests are rarely who they seem to be, and deep secrets often hide behind a smiling face. Key Features The Innkeeper's Burden: Take on the crucial role of the innkeeper, responsible for the well-being (and ultimate fate) of every soul who shelters under your roof. Choice and Consequence:  Prepare orders and listen closely to your strange patrons' grim stories, knowing your final decision affects the entire community. Psychological Tension: Experience a chilling atmosphere where trust is fragile, and paranoia is your constant companion. Unmask the secrets hiding beneath polite conversation. Medieval Horror: Immerse yourself in a dark and stylized medieval setting, where demonic entities and human cruelty intertwine.

Name: Tight Man
Supported languages: Cranial Explosions, Biological Shrapnel, and Gas! Tight Man is a fast-paced pixel-art action roguelike that takes high-risk, high-reward mechanics to the extreme. In this game, you don't fire bullets: you detonate your own head. Use your own biological remains to slaughter enemies in a room-clearing structure where every blast counts. Core Mechanics: Cranial Shrapnel: Your primary attack is a short-range explosion that hurls bits of brain and skull. The spread is erratic, forcing you to master positioning to be effective. Blood Harvest: Collect the blood left behind by fallen enemies to fill your meter and evolve during your run. Mutation Perks: Upon filling your blood bar, choose upgrades that alter your anatomy: make your brain chunks bounce, add explosive properties, or modify your blast radius (tighter for massive damage or wider for crowd control). Active Abilities: Unlock powerful active items and use your gas-propelled dash to maneuver through the chaos. Features: Visceral Combat: Feel every detonation as you coat the rooms with the remains of your enemies (and your own). Flesh Synergies: Create unique combinations by adjusting how your head shrapnel behaves to adapt to every challenge. Pure Roguelike: Permadeath, procedurally generated rooms, and a difficulty level that punishes mistakes but rewards boldness.
Average playtime forever: The game features cartoonish but frequent gore and violence. The main character's primary mechanic involves detonating their own head, resulting in blood splatter and biological debris (brain chunks). Players collect blood from defeated enemies to progress. There are no depictions of sexual assault, drug abuse, or self-harm.

Name: Exorcism of Montague Manor
Supported languages: A silent house. A single light. A choice that could kill you. Step into a pitch-black mansion where the only thing guiding you is a narrow beam of light — and the knowledge that using it may attract something you cannot see. Explore the halls, uncover hidden clues, and survive a psychological game of light and darkness where every decision feels uncertain. There is no visible enemy stalking you. There are no safe instructions. Only tension, silence, and the sound of the house watching you back. Each clue you collect triggers an unseen threat. A hidden timer begins, and you must decide whether to keep your flashlight on or turn it off — but the correct choice is never revealed. Hesitate, second-guess, or trust the wrong instinct, and the darkness will answer with a sudden, brutal shock. The mansion is alive with subtle environmental audio: distant whispers, creaking furniture, echoing footsteps, and unsettling noises that may or may not be real. Silence becomes as frightening as sound, and every corridor feels different in the dark. Key Features Psychological Light-Based Survival – Your flashlight is both protection and danger. Unpredictable Threat System – Hidden timers and randomized outcomes keep every clue tense. Shock Jumpscares – Rare but intense moments designed to make you physically jump. Dark Exploration – See what your light reveals. Dynamic Environmental Audio – Objects and rooms emit eerie sounds as you move through them. Minimal UI, Maximum Immersion – No hand-holding, no obvious warnings. Replayable Fear – Randomized events ensure no two runs feel the same.
Average playtime forever: This game contains depictions of violence, blood, frightening imagery, and intense psychological themes. Name: Piece of Ship
Supported languages: PIECE OF SHIP Piece of Ship is a chaotic first-person co-op game where your submarine is constantly falling apart - and it’s your job to keep it alive for just a little longer. Leaks. Exploding pipes. Electrical failures. Flooded rooms. You have duct tape , one wrench for the entire crew , and very little time . Fix the ship. Or drown trying. EVERYTHING IS BREAKING Your submarine is made of interconnected rooms and corridors. At any moment, something can go wrong: Cracked windows leaking water Pipes bursting under pressure Electrical systems failing or flooding Valves that must be closed carefully… or they’ll explode Failures appear randomly and more often with more players , forcing the crew to constantly move, adapt, and panic. PROXIMITY CHAT = PURE CHAOS Communication is your greatest weapon. And your biggest weakness. Piece of Ship uses proximity voice chat : If your teammate is in another room, they can’t hear you Someone must watch the control room screens Someone must actually run to the others and yell what’s wrong Expect shouting, confusion, and very bad decisions. ONE WRENCH. MANY PROBLEMS. There is only one wrench on the entire submarine. Remember where you left it Share tools Run through flooded corridors Trip over door thresholds while sprinting Get ragdolled by explosions and flying pipes Lose too much HP? Eat a SCHNITZEL and get back to work. No excuses. SOLO OR CO-OP (BUT REALLY… CO-OP) 1–4 players Solo play is possible Co-op is highly recommended for maximum chaos and fun Each run lasts around  15 minutes , ending either with: A barely functioning submarine Or a spectacular, watery failure “ONE MORE TRY” Piece of Ship is built around short, intense sessions that make you say: “Okay… one more try. This time we’ve got it.” You probably don’t. But you’ll laugh trying. Name: Don't PANIC!
Supported languages: Don’t PANIC! At its heart, this is a personal passion project. I've poured my creativity and effort into every system of this tactical space shooter, building a solid foundation for a vast journey. Rather than listing distant promises, I’m committed to delivering meaningful, frequent updates that steadily expand the universe. The foundation is strong, and the future is bright - No rush. No compromises. Step by step.   The Core Loop: Survive the Escalation Pilot your customizable combat ship in an open, seamless arena. Your goal is simple: survive, adapt, and outlast . But the longer you stay in the sector, the more intense the pressure becomes. Enemies arrive faster and grow more dangerous. The Threat Level is the heart of the experience. It controls enemy aggression, the scale of reinforcements, and directly drives the dynamic soundtrack that escalates with combat intensity (music by Karl Casey @ White Bat Audio ). Combat: Tactics, Chaos, and Control This is a fast-paced symphony of destruction where you are always outnumbered. Survival demands constant motion, sharp evasion, and smart arsenal management. Armor is a Puzzle: Every enemy has an armor level. Match your weapon's penetration to the target, or watch your shots ricochet in a spectacular— but wasteful —light show. Adapt or Be Overwhelmed: Choose between your Plasma Blaster, Autocannon or Lasercutter, and switch ammo types on the fly. Spam Smart Rockets into crowds, break locks with Flares, or use Energy Shield to deflect projectiles. Fire Control System provides a target lead indicator and armor readout—use it to make every shot count. What's In the Game Now? (Early Access Foundation) The core gameplay is implemented and highly replayable. The current version includes: A massive 10×10 sector arena with no loading screens Skill-based combat featuring armor penetration and ricochets A dynamic Threat Level system that makes the world react to your actions Flexible ship customization : primary and secondary weapons, defensive systems Varied enemies : fast interceptors, heavily armored units, missile platforms, and suicide drones Environmental hazards : damaging gas clouds that disable modules and chaotic wormholes Player progression : experience, levels, and stat upgrades A store for repairs, fuel, ammunition, and a firing range to test new weapons A Game Made to Be Played.  As a lifelong gamer, I built Don’t PANIC! with the same passion I feel when diving into my favourite titles. It’s not just my project — it’s my contribution to the community I’m part of. I hope you’ll feel that joy in every bullet‑hell moment and tactical decision you make. Early Access is an opportunity to play a solid, working foundation and watch the game grow: more content, more mechanics, more ways to die… and survive. If you enjoy arcade shooters, intense action, and constant danger — welcome aboard .

Name: Down the Dungeon
Supported languages: 'Down the Dungeon' is an unforgiving precision platformer that starts you from the top of the dungeon.  Without  checkpoints, navigate your way around dangerous traps, and rotting enemies - jumping and crawling through forgotten corridors. Collect 9  pieces of gear that provide powerful passives. Multiple main routes down to the bottom with branching hidden pathways. 3  consumable items. A throwable ember to illuminate the darkness, a dagger to slay creatures and jump on as a makeshift platform, and an apple that replenishes health- green of course. As you descend down the dungeon's multiple pathways, you will encounter increasingly more unforgiving platforming jumps and deadly traps; constantly testing your dexterity and precision. Between nerve-wracking jumps, you will encounter the undead -- previous adventurers that have tried to conquer these depths and failed. Kill them in any ways possible, using throwing knives, or the traps scattered amongst the dungeon. The ancient halls of the dungeons provide many secrets. Use throwing knives as platforms, embers to light the way, and apples to provide health all while crawling through dank corridors -- finding consumables and powerful gear to help you on your descent. The dungeon itself isn't hard enough for you? Try 'Hell Unleashed' or the elusive 'Bubble World' to further test yourself and your understanding of the dungeon. Will you be able to reach the bottom?

Name: Dead in Antares
Supported languages: Dead in Antares is a turn-based survival management game with RPG elements , set on an alien planet. Lead a crew of survivors sent on a mission to save humanity. Manage their needs, strengthen their teamwork, and explore this mysterious world to find a way back home. Earth is dying. In a desperate attempt to save it, ten highly trained specialists are sent into space as a final hope to find new resources that could save humankind. But after being swallowed by a mysterious wormhole that should not have been there, their ship crashes on an unknown and enigmatic planet . Call it fate, call it a miracle, they’re still breathing. But now, survival is their only option. Survival is more than just staying alive, it’s about managing every aspect of your crew and technology . Food, water, exhaustion, mental health, every system is deeply interconnected . Your ship may be in ruins, but its wreckage holds vital resources to help you build a functioning camp. Assign tasks wisely, repair and repurpose advanced equipment, optimize energy use, and make the most of every bits and pieces you may find. From a simple spaceship wreck to an exoplanet outpost , build and upgrade your work stations, be prepared for any outcome, and this planet should be (a little) less deadly. Your crew’s unique traits and personalities will shape your strategy. But beware, every decision can bring you one step closer to survival… or disaster . Dead in Antares is the ultimate evolution of the “Dead in” formula: pushing survival/management mechanics to their limits. Antares Prime is breathtaking, yet full of danger and mysteries. Beneath its hand-drawn landscapes lie dark secrets waiting to be uncovered. Was the crash just bad luck, or is there something more sinister at play? Survival won’t be easy: hostile forces lurk in the shadows. Engage in turn-based tactical combat , where every move counts.  Unleash your full potential with the brand-new Power Surge, an ultimate skill unique to each character that will turn the tide in your favor in combat. But you will have to venture deep into the unknown. Explore lush jungles teeming with life, scorching volcanic deserts, and eerie crystal forests hiding ancient secrets. Conduct research to understand the planet’s mysteries, gather crucial resources, and fight for your crew’s survival. Discover the truth about Antares Prime… if you can live long enough to find it. You’ll lead a crew of 10 playable characters , each with their own past, ambitions, and secrets . Pair characters together and uncover over 135 unique relationship dialogues . From respected crewmates to much deeper and complex bonds, each relationship will have its own surprises, bringing a bit of sweetness in this deadly world. A planet to save. Another one to explore. On Antares Prime, two factions have been at each other's throats for countless generations. One are the children of this land , tied to the ebb and flow of its complex ecosystem, highly adapted to its many wonders and dangers, free as the wind that runs inside their graceful exoskeletons. The others fell from the sky millennia ago , in an ancient spaceship. Clinging to their traditions, they proudly tried to subjugate what they saw as lesser species, through brute force and forgotten technologies… With moderate success. The story of Dead in Antares is filled with unexpected twists, and survival comes at a cost. Your choices will shape friendships, rivalries, and even betrayals. .. ultimately determining the fate of your crew and unlocking one of multiple endings. Will you unite them… or break them apart? Gorgeous hand-drawn 2D art, made by humans, for humans A mysterious planet to explore and study 2 factions to interact with, and their intricate backstories Survival and resource management at its best Deep story with tough choices, a home to save, an endless conflict to put an end to, and more! Up to 20 work stations to manage and more than 130 upgrades to craft! Full RPG progression system, with traits, levels, skills… The whole package! 10 characters to manage, each with unique traits Build the relationships between your characters! Every pair of main character has its own interactions. Tactical turn-based combat with over 60 battle skills to acquire Unleash their full potential with the brand-new power surge, ultimate skills that will turn the tide in combat 4 levels of difficulty so there’s a challenge for everyone (and of course, a 'True Captain' mode for the most hardened players!) Hours of story content, with 5 different endings Dead in Antares is the third installment of the Dead in series, after Dead in Bermuda and Dead in Vinland. All three games are standalones, but fans will be happy to find common threads and lore between them!

Name: Apocalypse: The Hunger
Supported languages: STOP MANAGING AN ARMY. START BECOMING A LEGEND. In the modern era of card games, the battlefield has become a spreadsheet. You hide behind walls of minions, calculating favorable trades and watching animations play out while you wait for your turn. It’s slow. It’s impersonal. It dilutes the kill. Apocalypse: The Hunger strips the genre down to its raw, violent core. We have removed the creatures entirely. There are no meat shields here. This is a Personal War . IMMERSIVE AUDIO: THE VOICE OF THE APOCALYPSE Don't just read the text— hear the threat. Fully voiced characters inject massive personality into every encounter. Whether it's the chrome-hardened slang of a Human merc, the guttural aggression of an Orc enforcer, or the raspy, radioactive whispers of a Ghoul , every race brings unique flavor to the fight. The soundscape is as lethal as the spells. The city doesn't just look dangerous; it talks to you. THE RETURN OF THE STACK Removing minions doesn't mean removing depth. We are bringing back The Stack —the gold standard of tactical interaction. Real-Time Counterplay: Don’t just watch your opponent play solitaire. Respond to their moves in real-time. Zero Decision Fatigue: Stop doing math on board states. Focus entirely on the immediate threat and the lethal spell in your hand. Visceral Impact: Every card played impacts your Hero directly. The tension is immediate, constant, and personal. THE EVOLUTION OF THE HERO’S JOURNEY The 'grind for packs' loop is broken. We replaced the static ladder climb with a true PVE RPG adventure set in the infinite, neon-soaked sprawl of Night City . Gear Upgrades: Don't just wish for a better card—discover one. Our Tradeskilling system allows you to upgrade items like legendary MMO weapons. Stats That Matter: You aren't just a life total. Your Strength, Agility, and apocalyptic attributes dictate how your deck functions. Build a stealthy rogue or a tanky juggernaut; your stats define your cards, not the other way around. TRUE ANTE: FEAR IS A MECHANIC In the Metropolis, survival is not guaranteed. We have resurrected the Hardcore Ante system. In key encounters, you aren't playing for XP—you are playing for your gear. Risk It All: Wager your rarest cards to access the city's depths and claim experimental technology. Real Consequence: If you lose, you lose the card. This creates a level of adrenaline that modern, 'safe' card games cannot replicate. EXPLORE THE ENDLESS SPRAWL Step out of the arena and into the streets. Our world-exploration system offers an endless urban landscape filled with procedurally generated encounters, secrets, and lore. Meaningful Stakes: Your choices in the city impact your deck’s capabilities. A Living World: This isn't just a menu of matches; it's a world you inhabit. Mathematical Uniqueness: We utilize roughly 101.3 Billion possible unique enemy deck combinations when generating the world. The likelihood of a game session being identical is distinctively slim—it is always a fresh run when playing Apocalypse: The Hunger . A RESPECTFUL ECOSYSTEM No Loot Boxes. No Gacha. No Gambling. Apocalypse: The Hunger rejects the vulturous mechanics of the genre. The Boxed Product Promise: A low entry price gets you the massive Core Game with 18 Starter Decks included. Precision DLC: Want a new playstyle? Buy a Specialized Pack . You get a complete playset (6 copies) of every card plus an Exclusive Card in that archetype. You never buy a random booster pack hoping for a rare drop. You buy exactly what you want, when you want it. The spreadsheet era is over. Welcome to the Apocalypse.

Name: Pelican Deep
Supported languages: In Pelican Deep, you're late for convent school and hoping the nuns will go easy on you. Remember your prayers, expose residual conversations, and navigate the disturbing choices presented to you.  Designed to be played in one 35-45 minute session, but depends on how much you explore and will save your game if you need to jump off early. Single-player. First-person. Features original soundtrack. As you continue through your school day, you will follow the nuns' orders as they become progressively more ominous and questionable. After generations of rehearsals, will you be able to break the loop, or will you succumb to the familial blueprint you were designed to act out?

Director of Solar Affairs is a turn-based strategy and simulation game centered on orbital combat, combining space warship design, construction, and solar system exploration . Beginning in 1935, the game spans several decades of warfare and scientific advancement, telling a space epic written by your own decisions. In the game, you assume the role of the Director of Solar Affairs , the highest authority of a world power’s space program. Over decades, you will oversee your nation’s expansion across the solar system—evolving from early 1,000-ton space destroyers armed with conventional cannons, to massive space battleships weighing tens of thousands of tons and equipped with large missiles and railguns, alongside multi-role scientific vessels. You will personally chart your nation’s path of expansion throughout the solar system. Core Gameplay Overview Design, build, and maintain space warships, scientific vessels, and auxiliary ships Allocate budgets to advance space technology Organize scientific exploration of alien planets Engage in space fleet battles of various scales against other nations when necessary Respond to a wide range of possible random events Improve your career rating through battlefield victories, technological progress, and exploration achievements, and write your own history of space expansion Game Features Turn-based space fleet combat on a hex-grid map Strategic turns progress on a monthly basis, allowing you to manage research, construction, exploration, and supply line maintenance outside of combat Gain funding through annual budget meetings and decide how resources are distributed between construction, maintenance, and research Freely design ships, with over 10 ship classes ranging from destroyers to battleships, and nearly 20 types of equipment and systems Invest in research to unlock higher-performance equipment and entirely new classes of space vessels Explore alien planets to uncover discoveries of strategic or scientific value Establish and maintain transport fleets and off-world supply lines Each nation features distinct ship designs, equipment, and national characteristics Play as the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, the Soviet Union, or Japan

Supported languages: The Manairons are back… and this time, they’re not staying quiet! Manairons is a 3D action platformer game set in the Pyrenees, where ancient legends mix with smoking factories, mischievous magic, and quirky little creatures. You are Nai, a manairó who has just awakened from centuries locked in the 'canut', a magical artifact as old as it is suspicious. A witch frees you (very timely, indeed) and gives you a mission: recover the 'canut' and stop the chaos it’s causing. The culprit? Llorenç, a landowner with zero charisma and a lot of machines. A Catalan fable inspires the world of Manairons, and the game is available to play in Catalan. A production by in collaboration with

Name: Little Toys
Supported languages: Here, it’s the toys themselves that face off in the most chaotic races ever seen! Every race is an unpredictable massacre: run, overcome obstacles, avoid traps, fly, snowboard down mountains, cross a child’s bedroom on a hoverboard, or surf through a water park. With 16 crazy tracks and dynamic weather offering over 12 different climates , no two runs are ever the same! Your goal? Finish first, no matter what. But in Little Toys, no one is ever safe. So cooperate… or sabotage each other, but never let the robots reach the podium! Nothing is more satisfying than seeing your friends lose their cool when you steal first place at the very last second. It’s funny, it’s unfair, it’s infuriating — and that’s exactly what makes every game of Little Toys unforgettable. Key Features Local multiplayer for up to 4 players – Challenge your friends, your family… even your grandma who’s never touched a controller. 16 unique tracks – From children’s bedrooms to snowy mountains, water parks, and more. What You Can Do Explore a large handcrafted open world filled with unique locations and points of interest Face the infected using firearms and melee weapons Drive vehicles and travel freely across the world Loot abandoned buildings and manage limited resources Discover environmental stories hidden in plain sight A World That Continues to Change ROTEN is being developed in Early Access to allow the game to grow alongside its community. It’s a relatively short game consisting of 50 levels. The game is inspired by a barrel-themed minigame from a well-known title featuring a tie-wearing gorilla. Gameplay Guide a fearless chicken from barrel to barrel until it reaches the final destination. Each level begins with the chicken loaded into a barrel. With a single click, you fire it into the air, launching it toward the next barrel in the sequence. Timing and precision are everything. Barrels don’t always stay still. Some move, rotate, or fire automatically, forcing you to adapt on the fly. Along the way, special barrels introduce new layers of control: some let you slow the chicken mid-flight, others allow you to adjust firing power, and certain barrels give you full control over the firing angle before launch. Levels are packed with hazards that must be avoided, from environmental obstacles to tricky layouts that punish careless shots. Portals add another twist, instantly teleporting the chicken across the level and challenging you to think spatially and plan your trajectory ahead of time. One wrong click sends the chicken flying off course but the perfect shot feels egg-cellent . Background Made by a Solo-Dev with love and care, I hope you enjoy the journey!

While exploring an abandoned industrial district you stumble across a mysterious, faceless building. Inside, among rusty shelving and forgotten folders, you find a dusty office. You have uncovered a portal to a digital past that was never meant to be reopened. Access the old terminal, explore its file system and interact with a text‑based interface reminiscent of DOS. Navigate corrupted files, decipher encrypted logs, access forbidden programs and uncover who — or what — was behind that screen. Every command you type reveals fragments of a buried story, one clue after another. Name: Competitive TicTacToe
Supported languages: You think you know Tic-Tac-Toe, right? Everyone does. It’s a simple game... or so we thought. We took the classic 3x3 grid and added one game-changing rule: When the board is full, your oldest piece disappears. This single twist turns that 'solved' game into a mind-bending strategy puzzle where every move counts. No more draws. No more boring stalemates. Every match has a winner. WHAT MAKES IT DIFFERENT? Picture this: You’ve lined up three marks. Victory seems certain. But wait—your very first piece vanishes, and suddenly your opponent has the winning line. That is Upgraded TicTacToe . You can’t just think about the next move; you have to think 3 or 4 moves ahead. You need to remember which piece is fading out next. It’s Chess-level thinking on a Tic-Tac-Toe scale. COMPETITIVE PLAY Ranked Matches: Play for glory and climb the ELO ladder. Start at 1000 points and work your way up. Every win counts, every loss teaches you a lesson. Casual Mode: Want to relax? Play casual matches to practice without the stress of losing rank. Global Leaderboards: See where you stand against thousands of players battling for the top spot. FEATURES 🚀 Lightning-Fast Matchmaking: Usually finds a game in under 10 seconds. 💬 Express Yourself: In-game chat with quick emojis. 📊 Deep Stats: Track your Wins, Losses, ELO, and Match History. 🤝 Play with Friends: Invite your Steam friends directly to a lobby. ⏱️ Quick Sessions: Matches take just 2-5 minutes. Perfect for a quick break. 🎵 Vibe: Clean, modern interface with non-intrusive background music. WHY DID WE MAKE THIS? Honestly? We were sick of Tic-Tac-Toe always ending in a draw. If you play against someone who knows what they're doing, the game is broken. We asked: 'What if the pieces didn't stay forever?' It turns out, that simple change fixes the entire game. No draws. Ever. Just pure strategy. WHO IS THIS FOR? If you love quick strategy games. If you love the grind of climbing a ranked ladder. If you want something that is 'easy to learn, hard to master.' THE BOTTOM LINE It’s Tic-Tac-Toe, but actually good. No draws, no RNG (luck), no pay-to-win nonsense. Just you and another player on a 3x3 grid. Simple concept. Deep strategy. Can you make it to the top of the leaderboard?

One moment you're threading through a horde by the skin of your teeth, salvation just out of reach. Then you grab the lightning powerup — and suddenly you're the horde. Supported languages: CULT OF THE SONS A Relentless Psychological Horror Anomaly Game In a remote manor house in England, a series of murders came to an abrupt end never solved, never explained. Every trace leads back to this place. Now you return. Not as a visitor, but as an investigator. CULT OF THE SONS is a psychological horror game designed to apply constant pressure on the player. CUSTOMIZABLE We want everyone to have fun. That's why you can choose whether you want monsters and jump scares before starting the game. You can also adjust the difficulty level. Atmosphere and Action The manor is not a static environment. Rooms change, objects disappear or reappear in different locations. Sounds, lighting, and details often feel subtly wrong just enough to create doubt. The game demands careful observation and trust in your own memory. Failure is rarely caused by slow reactions, but by hesitation and uncertainty. High-Variability Anomaly Gameplay Every round unfolds differently: Randomly occurring anomalies Unpredictable events Changes that only become apparent after multiple playthroughs There are no fixed routines and no reliable patterns. What you learn in one round may be useless in the next. Constant Threat The house is not empty. Creatures observe, follow, and react to your behavior. Some are clearly visible, others remain in the background. Not every threat announces itself and not every encounter can be avoided. Jumpscares are present , but used deliberately and with restraint. Tactical Glowstick System The player is given a deliberately limited tool: Green Glowsticks Mark seemingly safe areas Assist with orientation and comparison Red Glowsticks Mark suspicious zones Serve as a personal warning system If an area is marked inconsistently, the newer marker replaces the previous one. The system supports perception it does not provide safety. Difficulty as a Core Design Principle CULT OF THE SONS is not designed for casual play. Ten consecutive rounds Noticeably increasing intensity Growing psychological pressure The game is built to provoke mistakes. Progress is achieved through precise observation and self-control, not repetition. Features Psychological horror with a strong anomaly focus Dark, grounded environment Random events and environmental changes Pursuing enemies and controlled shock moments Tactical glowstick marking system High replay value For Players Who… Seek demanding horror experiences Understand and appreciate anomaly-based gameplay Are willing to engage with slow, sustained psychological pressure

Name: Animal Gaze on-XR
Supported languages: Animal Gaze on XR: A speculative archive exhibition   Animal Gaze is a digital and VR-friendly speculative archive exhibition based on the original story of the non-virtual exhibition of the same name held in Istanbul, Türkiye, in 2023. It contains multimedia artworks (some digitalized from physical art, some created digitally) by eleven participating artists from Türkiye, Canada and Germany. This collaboration between the Animal Gaze Project (AGP) and on-XR follows the same background story and conceptual limitations that shaped the initial project. The idea for the exhibition emerged from the imagination of a trial titled “Crimes Against Animals,” resulting in a speculative future where non-human animals are no longer treated as “natural resources” at the service of human beings for clothing, food, furniture, entertainment, cosmetics or medicine. In this future, the history of animal exploitation has become a thing of the past. The setting is a former slaughterhouse repurposed as a permanent exhibition space; the goal is to install an archival exhibition specifically for the animals of the future. Meanwhile, the human audience of today participates indirectly in this future confrontation, looking at what animals from the future have come to see and witnessing what their ancestors have been through. Each participating artist has created at least one piece intended to serve as a record for that future archive, creating an 'exhibition within an exhibition.' This speculative encounter finds its inspiration in Jacques Derrida’s reflections in The Animal That Therefore I Am . In his famous encounter with a cat, Derrida recognizes that the cat looks at him as much as he looks at her, prompting a consideration of the animal gaze, an aspect largely ignored in the history of Western philosophy. Realizing that animals possess an outward gaze that we cannot fully know leads to a crucial branching chain of thought: animals are no longer objects to be looked at, but subjects with their own gaze. This recognition is perhaps the most vital step for the liberation of animals; it offers a direct contrast to the way living beings are traditionally treated as a “heap” or a “flock,” denoted by numbers and classified according to their utility, some named as “livestock.” In this context, Animal Gaze asks: What if animals looked at their history of exploitation in a future where they were liberated? What would happen if we confronted the animals reflecting on their own past at an exhibition, and what would it mean to look at ourselves through their eyes? The interweaving of the present and the future through this shifting temporality raises urgent questions regarding the persistence of violence. Is this exploitation really a thing of the past, or is it still occurring the moment we step out the door? Are we carrying animal parts on our bodies right now, or trying to digest them in our stomachs? The artworks, while often appearing familiar, are intended to create an uncanny feeling within the context of an archive of exploitation. This sense of defamiliarization asks the audience to look at the “normal” from an entirely different perspective. In the context of this exhibition, the “animal gaze” does not intend to separate human beings by gathering the remaining animals under a single, monolithic category. Instead, it represents the encounter of the human animal’s gaze with the very thing the nonhuman animal’s gaze is directed at: the archive of their own exploitation. This is where all gazes, human and nonhuman, meet. The exhibition’s spatial journey is a deliberate curatorial choice designed to foster a post-anthropocentric way of being and relating to fellow creatures, as opposed to human exceptionalism. The first room contains no artworks where the visitor can meet the gaze of an animal. Visitors are guided to encounter this space, imagining how a cow or chicken might feel walking in here. In this room, the visitors are exposed to the space without any animal looking back at them, asking them to go beyond the traditional logic of the gaze. It is only as one moves toward the final room that the animals are seen looking back. While most of us are accustomed to seeing animals, it takes a shift in perspective to acknowledge the individual gaze of the Other who looks back. This approach challenges us to consider whether our way of looking is anthropocentric or if we can recognize each animal as an individual. It asks if we can put ourselves in their paws, hooves or feet, and questions which animals we recognize as individuals in contrast to those we mention only in terms of numbers and body parts.   Because this is an exhibition for nonhuman animals, human language is avoided in the artworks and exhibition as a whole. The archive avoids graphic imagery; it is considered a matter of ethical responsibility and respect not to show a fellow creature the details of how their ancestors suffered and died. Instead, the artists have considered the affective experience of the animal looking at these records. Finally, the curation accounts for varying physicalities, ensuring that the height and placement of works allow for different kind of animals to be able to see and experience the artworks.   Animal Gaze is a place of encounter and confrontation where humans and the marginalized, objectified, mythologized nonhuman animals arrive from two different dimensions of time to meet. Exhibition Artists: Ece Nada, Engin Arer, Havva Zorlu, İrem Yüksekbilgili, Jan Engelhardt, Kübra Ateş Sarı, Melisa Kılıç, Özlem Gök, Sara Ko, Shannon Johnstone, Volkan Parlak Exhibition Curator: Ece Nada Developer/Technical Artist: Engin Arer

Name: Peace Island
Supported languages: One fine day, in a remote island community off the coast of Maine, nine cats wake up to discover that their humans have disappeared. To survive, they must band together to uncover the mysteries of their storied island home - and ultimately, it is up to them to decide: Are the humans worth bringing back? - Explore a truly open world - The entirety of the island will be accessible, with each building containing a hand-crafted interior. No 'Invisible Walls,' or buildings with no purpose. - A realistic weather & tidal system - From foggy nights, to morning downpours, to clear, blue skies - you never know what those southeast winds might bring in - and you'll never want to miss a beautiful sunset! - Nine Playable Cats - Each with their own stories, preferences, skills, & weaknesses - as you get to know them, you'll know which one might be the best for a certain job! - Delve into a rich, 200-year alternate history - Learn family lineages, study old maps, and read books & letters better left hidden. - Your decisions matter! - How you approach life after humanity will decide how the game plays out in the end. - Replayability - Three different possible endings (and perhaps more!) - Experience a hand-crafted world - From the very beginning, we strove to create a world that isn't just 'that place between mission points.' The island might be small, but there is a LOT to discover and re-discover! - Original, adaptive soundtrack - From the mood of the cats, to the time of day, to the weather, the soundtrack changes. Each player's musical experience will be different! - An expanded emotional palette - Games are a wonderful storytelling - and all stories are not happy ones. - Relax! - Sometimes, you just want to hang out with the cats and watch the sun set. A mix of casual/slow gaming. - Meet new friends - and new enemies! - The humans might be gone, but old power structures remain. Currying favor with the deer might make the Seagulls less willing to talk! Peace Island began in November of 2017, when a Eric (a line cook) and Laura (a care worker) noticed a severe lack of rich, single-player, story-driven experiences in a game world where the major publishers were intent on developing the next open-world shooter. They knew it wasn't going to be easy - developing a video game of this size typically requires dozens of people and significant funding. They just had themselves, and whatever pocket change they could set aside after bills and rent. They worked on the project in whatever few hours they could set aside outside of their sleep and regular jobs. The world took shape, slowly but steadily. Occasionally, they could convince a friend to donate a piece of artwork, or save enough to hire a coder for an hour or two to help build the first, simple systems. From the very start, emphasis was put on crafting a beautiful world- one that would not simply serve as 'that space between one destination and another,' but as a place the player wants to linger in for just perhaps one more sunset. After two years of slow but steady progress, Peace Island 'went viral' in the fall of 2019, finally allowing the project to expand beyond a single bedroom, an outdated computer, and a few notebooks. Since then, the Peace Island project has expanded to include a a core team of 7, and an expanded talent pool of over 40 creatives from around the world. As we enter the fist days of our fifth year of development, we are more excited than ever to share the world & story of Peace Island.

With infrastructure down and conditions worsening, survival depends on using your training, equipment, and judgment to navigate the environment and stay alive. The world in Black Skies behaves in logical, real-world ways. Shelter blocks wind and cold. Fire produces warmth. Clothing insulates. Tools do what you expect them to do. The game is built around clear cause and effect, allowing you to reason through situations instead of memorizing abstract mechanics. What You Do Travel on foot through harsh terrain. Manage cold, hunger, thirst, fatigue, health, and mental state. Find shelter, build fires, scavenge supplies, and retrieve stashed gear. Decide when to move, when to stop, and how far to push based on conditions and risk. As you explore, you encounter cabins, sheds, equipment, and signs of prior human activity scattered throughout the wilderness. Situations develop naturally as you move through the world, and how you approach them is up to you. Key Features Realistic Survival Systems Warmth, hunger, thirst, fatigue, health, and mental state are simulated based on real-world human biology. Cold and Exposure as Core Threats Weather, wind, terrain, and timing directly affect survival. Preparation and awareness matter. Intuitive Interaction Objects behave as you expect. Containers hold items. Fires require fuel and ignition. Tools have practical, specific uses. Movement With Consequences Traveling consumes time and energy. Poor decisions increase danger, while good preparation improves efficiency. Usable Locations Cabins, sheds, and field shelters provide warmth, storage, and recovery without turning the game into a base-building sandbox. Emergent Situations Events and challenges arise through exploration rather than rigid scripting, allowing players to engage with the world at their own pace. Experience Black Skies is a deliberate survival game focused on realism, consistency, and meaningful decision-making. It is designed for players who want to survive by understanding their environment and responding to real conditions in a world that makes sense.
Average playtime forever: Black Skies contains depictions of survival in a post-collapse environment. Players may encounter themes such as environmental danger, injury, death, and human remains as part of a realistic survival setting. The treatment of mature subject matter is reviewed to ensure it is handled thoughtfully and responsibly, rather than sensationalized. The game does not include sexual content, sexual violence, graphic gore, or glorification of self-harm, drug abuse, or criminal behavior.
